symptoms: Small blister-like spots appear on leaves and twigs.
Young leaves wither and dry out.
Tender twigs die back and branches may dry up.
Black spots develop on flowers and fruits.
Infected fruit pulp becomes hard, cracks, and decays.
Young infected fruits shrivel and drop off the tree.
favourable_conditions: High humidity, frequent rains, and temperatures between 24 and 32 degrees Celsius help the disease grow.
prevention: Collect and burn all diseased leaves, twigs, and fruits.
Cover fruits on the tree with paper bags 15 days before harvest.
Use resistant or tolerant plant varieties.
Manage fruit flies to prevent late fruit fall and disease spread.
practices: Regularly inspect the orchard for signs of the disease.
Remove and destroy any infected plant parts.
Keep the field clean by removing dead twigs and debris where the pathogen lives.
Monitor the orchard to decide when control measures are needed.
